choices.misconception: I added all the tens digits and all the ones digits, 45 each, but forgot that the tens digits stand for tens.
I paired the numbers into sums of 110 but forgot the middle number, 55, which has no partner.
I added only the tens, $10 + 20 + \dots + 90$, and left out the ones digits.
I paired the numbers into sums of 110 but counted five pairs, although nine numbers make only four pairs and one left over.

hints: Add the first and the last number. Then add the second and the second-to-last.
Pair the numbers from the outside in: every pair has the same sum. Count the pairs and deal with any number left in the middle.

solutions.reliable: Pair the numbers from the outside in: $19 + 91$, $28 + 82$, $37 + 73$ and $46 + 64$ each make 110. That is $4 \times 110 = 440$, and the middle number 55 has no partner, so the total is $440 + 55 = 495$. The transferable idea: in a list that goes up in equal steps, pairing the first with the last gives equal sums.
solutions.elegant: The numbers go up by 9 each time, so their average is the middle number, 55. Nine numbers with average 55 add up to $9 \times 55 = 495$.

whyOnTest: Pairing numbers from the two ends of an evenly spaced list turns a long addition into one multiplication.
